title: Fast Entry SDK: conventions & mini-runbook (draft)
content:
Goal:
- Make a 3-5 minute "fast entry" path for new engineers and partner integrators so they can produce a working request and basic telemetry in under 20 minutes.
- Provide minimal conventions that keep sample apps small but production-representative (auth, retry, telemetry).

Audience:
- New hires on eng-developer-experience and solutions eng teammates running demos.
- Early-stage customers trialing Redwood API + client SDKs.

Non-goals:
- Full SDK reference (that's still in the spec repo).
- Heavy-weight onboarding for Dedicated/Private (those get a separate enterprise kit).

Overview of mini-runbook (workflow):
1) 2-min setup: install packages, export REDWOOD_API_KEY, run a single sample command that does a text generation.
2) 5-10 min: wire SDK into a tiny example (serverless function or single-page dev UI) with request/response, streaming toggle, and a simple error handling wrapper.
3) 3-5 min: enable telemetry probes (latency, token count, error code) and validate events appear in the sandbox console.
4) 5 min: smoke failure modes (rate-limit, network timeout) and show failover to a lower-cost model variant.

Key conventions (minimal, opinionated):
- File layout: src/index.ts, src/api.ts, tests/smoke.spec.ts, README.md. Keep example < 80 LOC.
- Auth: read REDWOOD_API_KEY from env, not in code. Use dotenv for local dev. Example: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY || 'local-insecure' (only in sandbox).
- Requests: wrap calls in a one-file helper with: setTimeout-based timeout, exponential backoff (max 3 retries), and request tagging header X-Example: fast-entry-v1.
- Telemetry: emit simple JSON "probe" messages to stdout in dev (timestamp, route, model, duration_ms, token_count, status). Hook these to the sandbox ingest in instructions.
- Streaming: default examples are non-streaming but include a single commented block showing how to subscribe to server-sent chunks.
- Model selection: default to a small open model from the catalog (explicit name in README) and include a single fallback model with lower cost.

Minimal sample: (pseudo)
- POST /generate -> call client.generate({model: 'rw-small-v1', prompt}) -> send 200 with text.
- If status != 2xx -> if 429 or 5xx attempt retry, else log and return 502.

Telemetry probes (practical):
- probe.request.started (route, trace_id, model)
- probe.request.completed (route, trace_id, model, duration_ms, tokens_in, tokens_out, status)
- probe.request.error (route, trace_id, err_code, err_message, retry_count)
Implementation notes: keep probes as single-line JSON to allow simple grepping in the example.

Local sandbox checklist (to validate before shipping sample to customer):
- [ ] Example runs with dockerless env (node 18, python 3.11 matrix).
- [ ] Probe events visible via sandbox ingest URL in README (make link configurable).
- [ ] CI smoke test (tests/smoke.spec.ts) asserts generation returns non-empty string and probe event fired.
- [ ] Network failure simulation documented: set REQUEST_FAIL_RATE=0.3 locally and exercise retry semantics.

Failure modes & demo scripts:
- Simulate 429: set MOCK_RATE_LIMIT=true -> show backoff path and eventual success after jittered retry.
- Simulate cold cache latency: add artificial 300ms delay server-side to demonstrate batching benefits in Optimize docs link.
- Simulate model mismatch: return structured error with code MODEL_UNSUPPORTED and show client fallback to rw-small-v0.

Onboarding quick tasks for solutions engineers (to teach during a 20-min call):
- Start the repo, run example in 2 minutes.
- Walk telemetry show: where to find probe lines, how to search by trace_id.
- Toggle streaming and demonstrate partial output.
- Trigger a 429 and show automatic backoff + how to alter retry policy.

Open questions / decisions pending:
- Small API ergonomic tweak: should SDK expose a one-shot request helper vs forcing streaming-first pattern? (impact: copy size of example)
- Default probe schema: do we include semantic user intent label in probe.request.start? privacy implications for end-users.
- CI smoke test flakiness policy: retry or mark flaky and monitor?

Links & artifacts referenced:
- Internal spec (Confluence): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/DEV/SDK+Conventions+Norms
- GitHub example repo draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/fast-entry-example (stub)
- Related PR for telemetry probe format: GH-PR: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/812
- Jira epics: DEVEXP-342, DEVEXP-388 (mini-runbook workstream)

Next actions (short-term):
- Riley: finalize the single-file helper with backoff and probe emission (ETA 3 days).
- Maya: author README play-by-play checklist and embed sandbox console link (ETA 4 days).
- Omar: add CI smoke harness and flaky-retry gating (ETA 6 days).
- Follow-up: schedule a 30-min dry-run with Solutions Eng and one external beta customer.

Notes to self (informal):
- Keep examples intentionally boring: fewer options = easier debugging in customer demos.
- Avoid advanced features in initial fast-entry (no function calling, limited tool use).
- Make README actionable: "If it doesn't work, run: curl -v http://localhost:3000/_diagnose"

Change log (draft history):
- 2025-10-20: initial sketch (Riley)
- 2025-11-03: added telemetry probes and failure modes (Maya)
- 2025-12-05: updated sample matrix and CI checklist (Omar)

End of mini-runbook (draft).

-- riley
